rv.q: Ifever a show had "big hit" written all over it then it is this wonderfully entertaining and deeply touching stage version ofthe successful British film The Full Monty.
This is crowdpleasing theatre - but with guts, wit and soul.
Masculinity in crisis has rarely been this much fun.

Daniel Evans directs it all with pacy aplomb, and ifthe eagerness to crowdplease ultimately comes at the expense ofsome ofthe film's poignancy, then the deliriously entertaining fmal strip club sequences are about as much fun as you're liable to have with your clothes on.
The final fabulous five minutes, when the men overcome all inhibitions and let rip, are a blinder - in every sense.
This is feel-good entertainment, impossible to dislike.
But in a play so astute about male vulnerability, it's a shame the female roles should be so scanty.
If another theater can be found, this raucous, cheeky crowdpleaser could run and run.
The show now hits the West End, after a national tour, with a considerable thump...
Whereas the Broadway musical was slick but heartless, the current dramatisation retains all the film's rough edges.
This is feel-good entertainment, impossible to dislike; yet at a deeper level it plays with our feelings of discomfort at this parody of male sexuality.
I'm unconvinced that this is anything more than high-value hen-night fare.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this crowd-pleasing stage adaptation, praising its warmth and entertainment value over the Broadway musical version. Some find the script workmanlike, but most agree it captures the film's heart while working well as live theater.
